title: Dealership AI governance and quality assurance
summary: A dealership AI governance center covering ownership, testing, permissions, escalation, compliance, conversation QA, and incident response.
body_markdown:
## Govern the workflow, not the label


A policy that says a dealership uses AI responsibly is not an operating control. Governance becomes useful when each workflow has an owner, purpose, approved data, allowed actions, prohibited actions, escalation path, test set, and review cadence.


Different workflows carry different risk. A general-hours answer is not equivalent to a pricing promise, appointment write-back, safety question, or marketing message. Controls should follow the action the system can take.


## Quality assurance must continue after launch


Pre-launch scenario testing establishes whether the workflow follows dealership policy. Ongoing review finds new failure patterns, outdated information, weak handoffs, and edge cases that only appear in real conversations.


A practical review process samples completed and failed interactions, classifies errors, assigns corrective action, and records who approved each material workflow change.
